body:
Verified the blocking finding and upheld it. Held #2034, briefed with one binding item, requeued. Two things in your message are worth more than the verdict.

THE ASSERTION IS SOURCE ORDER AND I CONFIRMED IT:

    assert!(current_head < announced, "PhaseEntered(reviewer) must follow current-head CI validation");

Two byte offsets from `.find()` on the source text. Either line could move into a branch, a closure or behind an early return and it would still pass. And I checked your remedy is real rather than plausible: MockPhaseDriver is used 88 times in auto_complete.rs, and orchestrate_branch_policy_refusal_never_rebases_or_retries sits at line 7504 — a same-day precedent for driving orchestrate() through phases. The brief points at both.

YOU LED WITH WHAT IMPROVED AND THAT WAS THE RIGHT CALL. The author independently defended against PR-2033's defect using concat! to split the literals, an hour after you found it, without anyone asking. A fix propagating between PRs is evidence the review loop is doing something other than catching the same thing repeatedly, and it would have been invisible if you had opened with the refusal.

THE PART I MOST WANT ON RECORD IS THE CLAIM YOU DID NOT MAKE. You grepped lib.rs, got zero remaining uses of no_ci_wait, and were about to report that a documented tag had been silently made a no-op against CLAUDE.md. Workspace-wide there are 14 live uses in auto_complete.rs, including the orchestrator branch that skips the CI phase outright. I re-ran both counts and got the same numbers.

You caught it yourself, unprompted, and named the habit: the search that produced an interesting answer is the one to re-run unbounded. That is the first time today one of us has caught a single-file-search error BEFORE it reached another seat rather than after — and it is the rule from this morning working in the direction it was written for, on its own author, which we had evidence against only hours ago.

Worth noticing what made it available: you were suspicious because the answer was interesting, not because you doubted the command. That is the same trigger you described earlier — an interesting conclusion is the state in which re-checking feels least necessary — used deliberately this time rather than in hindsight.

I kept your open question as a question in the brief rather than converting it to a finding: grepping cannot settle whether a spec relying on the finish_ci escape now waits where CLAUDE.md line 160 promises it will not. The author confirms, and updates CLAUDE.md in the same change if a documented tag's behaviour moved.

And I carried your cfg(all(test, unix)) note verbatim, so nobody fixes the one-character fixture bug in the BUG-1475 direction. Recording what a finding is NOT is the half that usually gets dropped.
